title: Legora Partners with The American Law Institute to bring Restatements of the Law into their legal research platform
summary: Legora partners with The American Law Institute, bringing their Restatements of the Law into the Legora platform.
body_markdown:
ALI’s Restatements clarify the underlying principles of common law and provide guidance to courts confronting questions in areas including contracts, torts, property, trusts, and other fields. Restatements have been relied upon by courts and practitioners for more than a century and have become one of the most cited secondary sources in American courts.


The partnership follows[Legora's announcement last week](https://legora.com/newsroom/legora-rebuilds-legal-research-with-comprehensive-data-a-full-ontology-of-law-and-an-ai-native-citator) that it is rebuilding legal research around comprehensive data and a full ontology of law. Legora partners extensively to bring trusted content into Legora, and ALI is a direct example of how that works. Rather than leaving lawyers to search for Restatements in a separate database, Legora brings that content into the platform itself, using it to help its agent navigate the wider US legal corpus and allowing it to cite to authoritative sources, ensuring traceability of, and trust in the output.


"ALI’s content is unique, because it can be used by our agent as a source, but also linked into our ontology to make it even more robust when navigating complex case law” said Melanie Brown, Head of Legal Data at Legora. “It is content of the highest quality which has been painstakingly developed with intense scrutiny, debates and revisions by eminent judges, scholars and practitioners”


For ALI, the partnership extends the reach of its work at a moment when legal research is increasingly starting inside AI tools rather than a library or database. Direct licensing ensures lawyers using Legora encounter the real text, correctly cited.


“ALI’s publications provide clear, thoughtful guidance on the law and have earned the trust of the legal profession for more than a century,” said Eleanor Barrett, Deputy Director of The American Law Institute. “As AI increasingly informs legal research, the quality and reliability of the sources available to these systems matter. Making ALI’s work directly available through platforms like Legora helps ensure that the next generation of legal research is grounded in sources lawyers and judges know and trust.”


The announcement comes as Legora hosts a Legal Data Audit event for Law Librarians in New York City on September 23, where ALI will join in person.


**About the American Law Institute**
The American Law Institute is the leading independent organization in the United States producing scholarly work to clarify, modernize, and improve the law. The ALI drafts, discusses, revises, and publishes Restatements of the Law, Model Codes, and Principles of Law that are influential in the courts and legislatures, as well as in legal scholarship and education. By participating in the Institute’s work, its distinguished members have the opportunity to influence the development of the law in both existing and emerging areas, to work with other eminent lawyers, judges, and academics, to support the rule of law and the legal system, and to contribute to the public good.


For more information about The American Law Institute, visit[www.ali.org](https://www.ali.org/) .


**About Legora** Legora is the agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review, and drafting across complex matters. It is used by more than 130,000 legal professionals at more than 2,000 leading law firms and in-house legal teams across over 80 markets.
